OS structureWhere do the OS services run?

    

      

        
        
      

    

    
Monolithic: every service inside the kernelone trip into the kernel and back · Linux, plus loadable modules

    
Microkernel: a tiny kernel, services run as user-mode serversmessages pass through the kernel, more trips · MINIX 3, seL4, QNX

    
Hybrid: some servers move back into the kernelWindows NT, macOS (XNU: Mach + BSD)

    
Linux

    
MINIX 3 · seL4 · QNX

    
Windows · macOS

    
Fewer crossings run faster; a smaller kernel survives a crashed driver

    
Golftheman, Public domain · recolored

System calls · recapOne instruction into the kernel: syscall

    

      
mov  $1, %eax         # 1 = write

      
mov  $1, %edi         # fd 1 = screen

      
lea  msg(%rip), %rsi  # the bytes

      
mov  $6, %edx         # "Hello\n" = 6

      
syscall

      
mov  $60, %eax        # 60 = exit

      
xor  %edi, %edi       # status 0

      
syscall

Pipespipe(): one buffer, two ends

    
C
int fds[2];
pipe(fds);     // fds[0] = 3: read · fds[1] = 4: write

    
empty → read() waits

    
full (64 KiB on Linux) → write() waits

    
no writer left → read() returns 0: end of file

    
A pipe is a kernel buffer that you reach through two file descriptors

    
Luca Galuzzi, CC BY-SA 2.5 · rules: man 7 pipe

./anonymous-pipe

PipesWho adds up 128 numbers?

    

    
    
main

    

    
One process per coreworker i computes the number i

    
After fork: separate worldsno shared memory, no way to talk

    
Each worker writes its numbermain reads; read() waits while the pipe is empty

    
sum in main

    
?

    
One pipe, many writers: the reader just waits until all have reported

Pipes · March 2022 · CVE-2022-0847Dirty Pipe: a bug in the pipe code

    

    
PAGE CACHE · /etc/passwd · READ-ONLY, OWNER ROOT

    

    
every program that reads this file sees this page

    
PIPE · A RING OF PAGE BUFFERS

    
    
splice(): the pipe points at the file's page, with no copyfast: the data never moves

    
flag CAN_MERGE, left over and never cleared

    
any user, no right to write the file
write(fds[1], buf, n);

    
write(): the bytes merge into that pagethe read-only file changes for everyone

    

    
Any user could become rootLinux 5.8 (2020) up to the fixes of February 2022 · Android phones too

    
Found by Max Kellermann while chasing corrupted log filesdisclosed March 7, 2022

    
Pipes share pages to be fast; one stale flag let any user write any file

    
Max Kellermann, “The Dirty Pipe Vulnerability”, dirtypipe.cm4all.com, March 7, 2022 · fixed in Linux 5.16.11, 5.15.25, 5.10.102 · the overwrite shown is illustrative
